However, it does not address the alternative auditctl configuration, which could leave the rule unenforced on systems that use auditctl.
review_concerns: Only augenrules path is handled; systems using auditctl will not get the rule applied.; No backup of the existing rules file before modification.
qa_verdict_reason: The plan only adds a standard audit rule file under /etc/audit/rules.d with appropriate permissions. This does not interfere with system services, networking, or authentication. Adding a watch on /etc/passwd is harmless and merely increases audit logging, which is the intended remediation. The check for existing content avoids duplicate entries. The limited scope (augenrules only) may leave systems using auditctl without the rule, but that does not cause instability.
qa_side_effects: Slight increase in audit log volume due to additional watch on /etc/passwd; Rule will only be applied when auditd is using augenrules; systems using auditctl will not get the rule
